The big question: 4790k or a 6700k.

For a similar price, the 6700k is a little bit better in most circumstances, but the real question is whether or not the peripheral PC components are worth the extra expense.

For instance, 32GB of DDR3 1600 cas latency 9 ram costs about $175, and 32GB of DDR4 2133 cas latency 9 ram costs $340. That's nearly double the price for far less than double the performance.

Is building a Skylake system worth the added expense for my price range?
Best PC for ZBrush under $1400 (already have a graphics card)

For zbrush, if given the choice between more ram and faster ram, get more ram. I wouldn't worry about latency too much. I mean, it may make a bit of difference, but not enough of one to break your bank or your budget for. You'll need at least 16GB of whatever you do decide on getting. I've got 32 GB, but my 'puter only sees 24, because two slots are dead :(. Anyway, with higher subdivision levels, memory requirements go up at a geometric rate. So, even if you upped your ram to 64 GB, you MIGHT get one more subdivision level out of it, and performance would still suck balls going that high.

I would recommend getting at least an i7 class CPU, but you don't need the newest or the best. In my experience, zbrush doesn't make use of multiple cores, and it rarely maxes out whatever core it's actually using anyway. I do all my rendering in other software, though.

As far as peripheral components, I own a medium sized intuos 3, a medium sized inutos 4 touch, and a cintiq 13HD. I use the intuos 3, almost exclusively. The touch surface on the intuos 4 just pisses me off, and I don't like my hand getting in the way of what I'm looking at on the screen with the cintiq. As well, my first tablet was an 18" intuos 3, and it was waaaaaaaay too fuckin' big. In practice, I probably use like a total of 3" of the drawing surface on any tablet. In all honesty, a bamboo would probably work just fine for zbrush.

ps stop by /v/zbursh anytime, it's lonely over there :(

I use a Cintiq 21UX, and I have a Cintiq 22 HD at the office. I have them attached to Ergotron LX arms. http://amzn.com/B00358RIRC.

I've had trouble getting any sort of real information about which types of performance optimizations make ZBrush work most effectively. Whenever I've run the "Test Multithreaded" benchmark within zbrush, it's always returned that my system benefited from multithreading, and when I run a processing-intensive operation like ZRemesher, it seems to consume all available processing on all cores. For ram, it's mostly seemed like when you don't have enough, the program simply stops working.

I'm going to go for at least 32GB of ram, and that encourages me to get the 6700k because I could upgrade to 64GB of ram at some point in the future.
